stem: A pharmacy discovers that several unused DEA Forms 222 are missing. What is the first regulatory response?

choices.text: Immediately report the loss to the responsible DEA Special Agent in Charge with available form details.
Use the out-of-state prescription rule when its schedule, age, and verification conditions have not been checked.
Process another refill because an authorization written by the prescriber overrides schedule limits.
Treat the request as an insufficient-stock partial fill and use the 72-hour remainder rule.
Handle the drug or transaction as ordinary Massachusetts Schedule VI activity.

explanation.core_reasoning: A registrant must immediately report lost or stolen used or unused DEA Forms 222 to the responsible DEA Special Agent in Charge and retain the required replacement-form statements. The pharmacy must use the exact trigger and deadline rather than borrowing a nearby controlled-substance rule.

choice_analysis.A: This applies Lost or stolen DEA Form 222 reporting: A registrant must immediately report lost or stolen used or unused DEA Forms 222 to the responsible DEA Special Agent in Charge and retain the required replacement-form statements.
choice_analysis.B: That choice belongs, if at all, to Out-of-state Schedule III through VI prescriptions; its trigger does not match this scenario.
choice_analysis.C: That choice belongs, if at all, to Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits; its trigger does not match this scenario.
choice_analysis.D: That choice belongs, if at all, to Schedule II partial fill caused by pharmacy inability; its trigger does not match this scenario.
choice_analysis.E: That choice belongs, if at all, to Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription-drug status; its trigger does not match this scenario.

related_facts: A registrant must immediately report lost or stolen used or unused DEA Forms 222 to the responsible DEA Special Agent in Charge and retain the required replacement-form statements.
explanation.mpje_trap: Applying schedule vi to facts controlled by lost forms.
